cases.question: When should we fail over to the secondary payment provider during a SEV1?
cases.answer: If the primary PSP (Stripe) error rate is above 10%, fail over to the secondary PSP (Adyen) with the feature flag `payments.psp.failover` [1]. Rollback takes about 4 minutes and does not require approval during a SEV1 [2]. Severity: SEV1; Definition: Checkout failing for more than 5% of requests; Response time: 5 minutes; Who is paged: Payments on-call and incident commander [3].

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.section: Payments Service Incident Runbook > First response for SEV1
sources.text:
1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
2. Open an incident channel named #inc-payments-<date>.
3. Check the PSP status dashboard. If the primary PSP (Stripe) error rate is above 10%, fail over to the secondary PSP (Adyen) with the feature flag `payments.psp.failover`.
4. Post a status update every 30 minutes until resolved.

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.text: Deployments to the payments service are rolled back with `deployctl rollback payments --to previous`. Rollback takes about 4 minutes and does not require approval during a SEV1.

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.section: Payments Service Incident Runbook > Severity levels
sources.text:
| Severity | Definition | Response time | Who is paged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEV1 | Checkout failing for more than 5% of requests | 5 minutes | Payments on-call and incident commander |
| SEV2 | Elevated latency (p95 above 2 s) or a single PSP down | 15 minutes | Payments on-call |
| SEV3 | Degraded non-critical feature (refund emails, receipts) | Next business day | Ticket only |

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.text: A blameless postmortem is due within 5 business days for every SEV1 and SEV2.

2. Store it in Vault under `secret/services/<service>/api-key`.
3. Deploy with dual-key support, then revoke the old key after 24 hours.

sources.section: Payments Service Incident Runbook > First response for SEV1
sources.text:
1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
2. Open an incident channel named #inc-payments-<date>.
3. Check the PSP status dashboard. If the primary PSP (Stripe) error rate is above 10%, fail over to the secondary PSP (Adyen) with the feature flag `payments.psp.failover`.
4. Post a status update every 30 minutes until resolved.

sources.text: Company laptops must have full-disk encryption and automatic screen lock after 5 minutes. Personal devices may access email and Slack only through the managed mobile app.

sources.title: Vendor Contract Playbook
sources.text: Any vendor touching customer data must sign the Halcyon DPA and provide a SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent.

sources.title: Performance Review Process
sources.text: Halcyon runs two review cycles per year: a mid-year check-in in July and a full annual review in January. Only the annual review affects compensation.

sources.title: Travel and Expense Policy (2026)
sources.text: Nightly hotel caps are 275 USD in high-cost cities (San Francisco, New York, London, Tokyo) and 200 USD elsewhere.

sources.title: Parental Leave Policy (2026)
sources.text:
Primary caregivers receive 20 weeks of fully paid leave. Secondary caregivers receive 10 weeks of fully paid leave. Leave can be taken in up to three blocks within 12 months of the birth, adoption or foster placement.

| Caregiver type | Paid weeks | Blocks allowed | Must be used within |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | 20 | up to 3 | 12 months |
| Secondary | 10 | up to 3 | 12 months |

sources.title: Customer Security FAQ
sources.text: Robot telemetry is retained for 13 months by default. Enterprise customers can set retention between 30 days and 7 years.

sources.title: Parental Leave FAQ (2023)

sources.text: Yes. Employees must complete 6 months of service before becoming eligible for paid parental leave.

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.section: Payments Service Incident Runbook > First response for SEV1
sources.text:
1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty within 5 minutes.
2. Open an incident channel named #inc-payments-<date>.
3. Check the PSP status dashboard. If the primary PSP (Stripe) error rate is above 10%, fail over to the secondary PSP (Adyen) with the feature flag `payments.psp.failover`.
4. Post a status update every 30 minutes until resolved.

sources.title: Payments Service Incident Runbook
sources.section: Payments Service Incident Runbook > Severity levels
sources.text:
| Severity | Definition | Response time | Who is paged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEV1 | Checkout failing for more than 5% of requests | 5 minutes | Payments on-call and incident commander |
| SEV2 | Elevated latency (p95 above 2 s) or a single PSP down | 15 minutes | Payments on-call |
| SEV3 | Degraded non-critical feature (refund emails, receipts) | Next business day | Ticket only |
